subject: NovaHealth POC: assessment route & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@novahealth.com>, Dave Russell <dave.russell@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: NovaHealth POC: assessment route & next steps

Hi Sarah / Dave —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight route for a 6-week POC so we can align on success criteria and the evaluation approach before we spin up infra: 

1) Goal: Validate Redwood inference for NovaHealth clinical note extraction and intent classification with production-like latency and at least X-quality on entity extraction (we'll define X below).

2) Two-step evaluation recommendation (proposed):
   - Phase A (offline assessment, 1 week): run a seeded offline evaluation on NovaHealth-provided, de-identified samples to validate correctness and tune prompts/response format.
   - Phase B (shadow validation, 3 weeks): short shadow run against a small, live stream of traffic (read-only, no PHI persisted on Redwood) to surface integration issues and latency under production cadence.

Why both? Offline lets us iterate quickly on edge-case coverage without traffic risk; shadow gives real-latency and human-in-the-loop validation. If compliance prevents shadow, we can extend offline and add more rigorous sampling.

3) Suggested acceptance gates (draft) — we should finalize these together:
   - Extraction F1 >= 0.86 on gold labels (Phase A)
   - Intent classification precision >= 0.90
   - 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 350ms (dev region)
   - No more than 2 critical misclassifications in a 48-hour shadow window

4) Timeline & owners (draft):
   - Week 0: agreement on dataset and access (owner: NovaHealth PM)
   - Week 1: Phase A offline runs + rubric (owner: Kimberly / Redwood eng)
   - Weeks 2–4: Phase B shadow (owner: NovaHealth engineering + Redwood SRE)
   - Week 5: Final analysis & decision (mutual)

5) Data & security: please confirm whether the sample traffic can be de-identified or whether you require Redwood Private (VPC) for the shadow window. We can provide an SSO/KMS checklist if needed.

Attachments: I attached a short playbook + a dataset schema stub for your PM to complete.

Next step: can you confirm the PM owner, preferred eval metric priority (if different from the draft), and whether shadow is allowed from a compliance perspective?

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
(Attachment: redwood_poc_playbook.pdf, nova_poc_dataset_schema.csv)

Thanks, Kimberly — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PM owner: I will loop in Priya (PM) — she owns integration and will provide the dataset schema.
- Security: we prefer not to send PHI for the offline dataset. We can provide de-identified clinical notes (redacted identifiers) for Phase A. For shadow (Phase B) the compliance team is cautious; they'd prefer Redwood Private (VPC) unless you can guarantee no token persistence and a SOC2 + HIPAA BA in place. Please confirm Redwood's policy on short-term shadowing without a Private deployment.
- Success metrics: the extraction F1 is the primary metric. We also care about hallucination rate (free-text insertion) — would like hallucination < 3% on sampled outputs.

Also attaching a quick access matrix with who will approve environments.

Sarah Lin
Head of Product, NovaHealth
sarah.lin@novahealth.com

Sarah — thanks for the fast reply and the access matrix. Per your notes, here's a revised, operational playbook and a concrete grading rubric so we can lock on what gets counted in Phase A vs Phase B.

High-level: keep Phase A as strict offline scoring; treat Phase B as validation for latency, edge cases, and human-acceptance. If compliance requires Redwood Private for shadow, we will surface a Private deployment estimate in parallel; otherwise we can run a restricted shadow in our hosted environment with no persistence and ephemeral logs (we can provide an audit config).

Attached: redwood_poc_playbook.pdf (2-page) — important excerpts below.

POC playbook (excerpts):
- Data intake: NovaHealth provides up to 2,000 de-identified notes for Phase A. Format: CSV with columns: note_id, text, gold_entities (json), intent_label.
- Offline eval flow: 3 seeded runs with incremental prompt variations; record precision/recall/F1 per entity type + hallucination checks (sampled manual review).
- Shadow flow: route 2–5% of live traffic to Redwood read-only endpoint for 3 weeks; Redwood will expose a dashboard with per-request latencies and failure rates.

Scoring rubric (Phase A):
- Primary: Entity extraction micro-F1 (weighted average across entity types) — PASS if >= 0.86.
- Secondary: Intent precision (macro) — PASS if >= 0.90.
- Hallucination: sampled rate <= 3% — PASS if <= 3%
- Formatting/structured output compliance: 100% success on required fields (no free-text where structured expected).

Acceptance decision logic:
- Green: all PASS metrics -> proceed to production plan discussion.
- Yellow: one metric fails but dev fixes estimated < 2 weeks -> iterate (additional 1-week offline run).
- Red: multiple core metrics fail or hallucination > 6% -> stop and re-scope.

Timeline proposal (updated):
- Week 0 (this week): sign data access & confirm PM owner (NovaHealth) -> action: Priya to fill schema by Thu 9/17
- Week 1: Phase A runs (Redwood to run three seeded offline experiments) -> deliverable: offline report + issue tracker
- Week 2–4: Shadow (if allowed) or extended offline sampling -> deliverable: shadow dashboard + human-review notes
- Week 5: Final review + pass/fail decision meeting

Owners (Redwood): Kimberly (AE, overall), Marissa (Solutions, prompt engineering lead), Marcus (SRE, shadow infra).

Quick ask: Priya's email + confirmation on whether NovaHealth compliance will allow a hosted shadow with ephemeral logs or if we must provision Private. If you need, I can add our Security checklist and a short SOC2/HIPAA attainment summary.

Thanks — looking forward.

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_poc_playbook.pdf)

Looping in a couple of quick operational notes from infra/SRE perspective: 

- Shadow sample size: for latency signals we recommend routing a minimum of ~1,000 requests/day across the shadow window to get stable p95/p99. If NovaHealth traffic is lower, extend shadow duration instead of increasing percent.
- Batching & concurrency: for fairness with production, we'll mirror your concurrency but can suggest batch sizes; please share typical request QPS.
- Resource annotation: if Private is required and timeline is tight, we can provision a short-term dedicated node pool (estimate 3–5 business days after sign-off).

I'll prepare a short infra checklist and cost delta for Private vs hosted shadow and drop it in the Drive link Kimberly shared.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin, SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
